description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NSF NHERI 2024: Assessment of Fire Sprinkler System in a 10-Story Cold-Formed Steel Building During Seismic Loading Scenarios is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Leah Seifert, California Polytechnic State University San Luis Obispo (calpoly.edu). Fire sprinkler systems are intended to save lives and reduce building damage caused by after-earthquake fires. Fire sprinkler (FS) systems can better withstand seismic forces through the utilization of fire sprinkler codes, building codes, and numerical models to aid in the design layout and overall to improve seismic performance. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 3 top-level files (PDF). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-rn6t-xq10. Keywords: NSF NHERI UCSD LHPOST6, CFS, Non-structrual, Seismic Performance. Published 2024-08-28. Facility named: Six Degree of Freedom Large High-Performance Outdoor Shake Table (LHPOST6) - University of California, San Diego. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
